title: Standards baseline before promoting a provenance-carrying distributed observation fabric
question: Which existing open standards and reference implementations already cover the six elements of the proposed KUEPER Distributed Observation Node / Constellation Fabric — heterogeneous node observation metadata, provenance and uncertainty, time/position synchronization, store-and-forward operation, versioned fusion state claims and a confidence-aware dashboard — for example OGC SensorThings API, SOSA/SSN, O&M, W3C PROV, STAC, MQTT Sparkplug B, Eclipse Ditto/EdgeX and Apache Kafka, and what concrete gap would the KUEPER fabric actually have to fill rather than reimplement?
why_now: The research-watch entry's explicit next gate is to compare existing open standards/platforms for sensor metadata, provenance, geospatial observations and distributed edge messaging before promotion to a product candidate. The advanced-products track lists distributed passive sensing and MiniNode swarm platforms as watch areas, so the candidate remains blocked on this comparison and risks duplicating mature standards.
real_world_anchor: OGC SensorThings API / SOSA-SSN / O&M, W3C PROV, STAC, MQTT Sparkplug B, Eclipse Ditto/EdgeX, Apache Kafka and peer-reviewed sensor-web interoperability literature
novelty_reason: This is an architecture/standards state-of-the-art question, not a rephrasing of the photophoretic lift, drip-emitter hydraulics or MiniNode T/RH metrology topics. It resolves the explicit next gate in the research-watch file and tests the product thesis's novelty claim against existing standards.
